note: DRAFT positional playbook for employment agreements governed by Indian law. Covers notice period, non-compete, non-solicit, IP assignment, severance, probation, and governing law. Indian Contract Act s.27 makes post-term non-competes unenforceable — the starting position is always no non-compete. No in-house lawyer has approved these positions.
not_legal_advice: Every finding is a POTENTIAL_ISSUE against a company standard, not a statement of law.

rules.why: Notice period from employee side. 30 days is standard; 60-90 days for senior roles. No dealbreaker since longer notice protects the company. Uses equals because years() parser does not handle day values.
Notice period from employer side. Should match or exceed employee notice for fairness. 30 days standard; 60 days for senior roles.

starting.text: No post-term non-compete (Indian Contract Act s.27)

rules.why: Post-term non-competes are unenforceable under Indian Contract Act s.27 (Niranjan Shankar Golikari, Superintendence Company of India). The starting position is NO non-compete. Any non-zero duration crosses the dealbreaker. During-term non-competes are acceptable and handled by the flat playbook.
Non-solicitation (of clients/employees) is more enforceable than non-compete under Indian law, but still read narrowly. 6 months is reasonable; 1 year is market. Above 2 years is excessive.
Probation period. 3 months is standard; 6 months for senior/specialist roles. Above 1 year is unusual and may be challenged as unfair.

starting.text: IP created in course of employment only

rules.why: IP assignment should be limited to work created during and in the course of employment. Blanket assignment of all IP (including personal projects) is overreaching and may not hold up.
Employment in India must be governed by Indian law. Indian labour legislation is mandatory and cannot be contracted out of.

Severance beyond statutory requirements. No extra severance is the starting position for most employees. 3-6 months is standard for CXO-level. Above 12 months is a golden parachute that needs board approval.
